Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Third Quarter 2024 results. With me on the call are Lisa Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team, including Sarah Lopez, our Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Lisa Chen.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects: overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Patel to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. As Lisa mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.8 billion, representing a 5.1% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by supply chain efficiencies and pricing discipline. Operating income was strong, reflecting cost management. Diluted earnings per share were $1.52. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining GCB's third quarter fiscal 2024 earnings call. As a reminder, all figures we discuss today are in USD, and reconciliations to GAAP can be found in our earnings release and 8-K filed this morning.

Starting with the headline numbers: Q3 delivered a strong performance amid a resilient yet challenged macroeconomic backdrop. Net sales reached $15.8 billion, up 5.1% year-over-year, driven by 6.2% organic sales growth—a 120 basis point beat against our prior guide. This was fueled by a healthy mix of 2.8% volume/mix growth and 3.4% pricing actions, marking our sixth straight quarter of positive volumes globally. Diluted EPS from continuing operations came in at $1.52, up 10.3% on an underlying basis, exceeding our $1.45 consensus by $0.07. These results reflect the strength of our Everyday Essentials portfolio—think our flagship PeakPure water brands, Zestify snacks, and Lumina personal care lines—which continues to outperform in a high-inflation environment where consumers prioritize value-for-money staples over discretionary impulse buys.

Diving deeper into segment performance: Food & Beverages, which is 52% of sales, saw organic growth of 7.1%, with volumes up 3.2% as our nutrition-focused innovations like the reformulated PeakFuel protein bars gained 1.2 share points per Nielsen data in North America. Pricing contributed 3.9%, partially offsetting cocoa and palm oil inflation that peaked at +25% YoY. Snacks sub-segment was a standout, mirroring Frito-Lay's resilience, with e-commerce penetration hitting 18%—up from 12% last year—thanks to our Amazon Velocity partnership.

Health & Beauty, 28% of sales, posted organic sales +5.8%, led by 4.1% pricing to recover input costs in surfactants and packaging, while volumes held flat amid softer skincare demand. Our Lumina Clean Beauty line, positioned against The Ordinary and CeraVe, drove 15% category growth via premiumization trends, capturing affluent millennials trading up despite economic headwinds.

Household Essentials, 20% of sales, delivered a robust 6.5% organic growth, with volumes +2.9% on the back of our eco-refreshed PeakClean detergents. Laundry and cleaners benefited from share gains versus private label, which per IRI scans grew only 1.8% in the quarter versus our 4.2%.

Regionally, North America contributed 45% of sales with 4.8% organic growth, bolstered by targeted trade spend optimization and in-store execution that lifted ACV distribution to 98%. EMEA delivered 8.2% organic, our strongest region, driven by pricing discipline in a +10% inflation market and strong performance in the UK and Germany, where our beverages outpaced Coca-Cola's local volumes. APAC grew 5.9% organically, with China rebounding +12% post-COVID restrictions via our localized PeakTea ready-to-drink line, though FX headwinds shaved 2 points off reported growth. Latin America was softer at +3.1% organic, pressured by Argentina's hyperinflation and Brazil currency volatility, but we see stabilization ahead.

On margins, we expanded gross margin to 48.2%—up 190 basis points YoY—through supply chain efficiencies from our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout, which unlocked $250 million in procurement savings YTD via AI-driven supplier negotiations and dynamic sourcing from Southeast Asia. This more than offset $180 million in raw material inflation. Underlying operating margin reached 18.4%, +110 bps, reflecting disciplined SG&A at 29.8% of sales, aided by zero-based budgeting and a 15% reduction in agency spend through in-house digital content studios. Adjusted free cash flow was $2.1 billion for the quarter, up 22%, supporting $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a 12% dividend hike announced today—our 47th consecutive increase.

Strategically, we're accelerating our "Power Brands, Powered by Tech" initiative. We've launched GenAI pilots in demand forecasting with Palantir, reducing stockouts by 25% in our North American DC network, and invested $400 million in sustainable packaging—60% recycled content across beverages by year-end, aligning with EU Plastic Pact mandates and consumer preferences per Kantar data, where 72% of Gen Z prioritize eco-claims. M&A remains opportunistic; we closed the $1.1 billion acquisition of VitaGlow probiotics last month, adding 400 bps to Health & Beauty EPS accretion in FY25, while divesting non-core pet foods for $450 million to sharpen focus.

Before moving on, I'd like to address competitive activity and our responses, as this has been a dynamic area shaping our performance across the CPG landscape. Our industry is hyper-competitive, with high-velocity SKUs, relentless innovation, and shifting consumer preferences driving constant pressure on market share, pricing, and margins. We've seen elevated activity from both multinational peers and aggressive private label expansions, but our disciplined responses have allowed us to protect our core franchises while accelerating growth in high-margin segments.

According to the latest IRI and Nielsen multi-outlet scans for the 52 weeks ending September 30th, total CPG dollar sales grew 4.2% industry-wide, but volume growth lagged at just 1.1%, reflecting persistent inflation and trade-down behaviors. Market share remains fragmented, with the top 10 CPG players holding about 42% in North America, down 20 basis points YoY due to retailer own-brands and DTC disruptors. Our key rivals—Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and Reckitt—have been particularly aggressive, launching over 150 new products in household and personal care alone this quarter, emphasizing sustainability claims and clean-label formulations to capture the premiumization trend.

In North America, which represents 55% of our revenue, P&G's Tide Pods Eco-Refill initiative has been a standout, driving a 3.2% dollar share gain in liquid laundry detergents to 28.5% ACV. This pod format, with its 40% recycled plastic packaging, resonated amid consumer sustainability surveys showing 68% prioritizing eco-friendly options—up from 52% two years ago. Similarly, Unilever's Dove Body Wash "No Parabens" relaunch pressured our Simple brand, where we saw a temporary 1.8% volume dip to 14.2% share. Private labels from Walmart's Great Value and Kroger's Simple Truth compounded this, expanding 6.5% in units sold, capturing 22% of the category as shoppers traded down amid 7-9% pricing inflation on branded items.

Over in EMEA, 25% of our mix, competitive intensity ramped up with Nestlé's Garden Gourmet plant-based expansions and Henkel's Persil Bio Color launch. Nestlé gained 150 bps in meat alternatives, hitting 12.4% value share, fueled by a 15% A&P uplift tied to TikTok influencer campaigns targeting Gen Z. We felt this in our Amy's Kitchen organic frozen meals line, where velocity softened 4% in the UK and Germany. Regional commentary here: EU regulations on green claims have leveled the playing field somewhat, but discounters like Aldi and Lidl grew private label penetration to 32%, squeezing branded shelf space by 2-3 feet per store on average.

APAC and LatAm, our growth engines at 20% combined, saw even fiercer battles. In China, via our Tmall and JD.com partnerships, Procter & Gamble's Olay "AI-Powered Skincare" app-integrated line stole 2.1% share from our Pantene and Head & Shoulders franchises via hyper-personalized recommendations, boosting repeat purchase rates 22%. In Brazil, Unilever's Rexona antiperspirant "Active Shield" promo blitz, offering 2-for-1 BOGO deals, eroded our Degree share by 90 bps amid a 12% category inflation spike.

Now, turning to our responses—these have been multifaceted, data-driven, and yielding tangible results. First, on pricing and trade: We implemented targeted Everyday Low Pricing resets on 35% of our portfolio, averaging 4-6% list price increases but layering in 12% more trade spend to fund retailer-funded promotions. This preserved our average selling price at $3.42 per unit, up 5.2% YoY, while improving distribution to 92.6% ACV—gaining 110 bps. In laundry, we countered Tide with our Gain Flings "Bio-Boost" variant, hitting shelves in 85% of top U.S. chains within 6 weeks, which reversed that 1.8% volume dip to a 0.9% gain, with household penetration jumping 7% via IRI facts.

Innovation has been our sharpest sword. We accelerated our pipeline by 20%, launching 28 SKUs this quarter versus 22 planned. Highlights include our "PureEarth" household cleaner line—plant-derived, 100% recyclable, and EWG-verified—which captured 3.4% share in all-purpose cleaners within 90 days, outpacing Clorox's Green Works relaunch. In beauty, our "SmartScent" body mist tech, using micro-encapsulation for 8-hour release, drove a 14% velocity uplift in APAC, clawing back 1.5% share from Dove. These initiatives are backed by $450 million in A&P, up 8% YoY, with 40% digital—think Shopify DTC trials yielding 25% higher basket values and our Roblox metaverse activations reaching 5 million Gen Z impressions.

Regionally tailored: In EMEA, we partnered with Carrefour and Tesco for exclusive "Health Halo" endcaps on our organic snacks, boosting facings by 15% and growing share 2.3% despite private label pressure. In LatAm, we leaned into omnichannel with Mercado Libre integrations, where our Degree saw an 18% e-comm sales surge via AR try-on filters. And in North America, our Walmart Club-exclusive bundles on Flamin' Hot snacks countered Frito-Lay's 10% promo volume, stabilizing salty snacks share at 19.8%.

Strategically, we're not just reacting—we're reshaping the battlefield. Our "Velocity 2.0" program uses AI-driven predictive analytics from SymphonyAI to forecast competitor moves 4-6 weeks ahead, optimizing trade allocation for a 15% ROI uplift. We're also doubling down on core 15 brands, which grew 6.1% versus 2.8% for the rest of portfolio, focusing on "hero SKUs" with 2x category velocity. Sustainability is table stakes now; our 2025 Scope 3 emissions cut to 25% positions us ahead of Unilever's 30% target, winning ESG investor flows. Finally, M&A scouting targets bolt-ons in pet care and RTD beverages, where private equity-backed players like Mars and Monster are vulnerable.

Quantitatively, these responses delivered: We gained 40 bps overall market share to 7.2%, with organic sales +5.4% (2x industry), gross margins expanding 110 bps to 48.2% despite input costs up 6%. Trailing 12-month ROS hit 14.8%, best in class.

Looking forward, we expect competitive activity to intensify with back-to-school and holiday ramps—P&G's rumored $1B media blitz looms large—but our fortified moats in distribution, innovation, and consumer insights give us confidence. We'll continue monitoring IRI weeklies closely and adjusting dynamically.

As we think about brand performance and innovation, which is a key growth engine, in the CPG space where category growth has hovered around low-single digits globally per Nielsen data, innovation remains our North Star for outpacing the market. We've delivered 12% organic sales growth from new products this quarter, representing 25% of our total top-line, up from 18% a year ago. This is ahead of the industry benchmark of 15-20% from IRI's New Product Pacesetters report, and it's driven by a disciplined pipeline that's laser-focused on megatrends like health & wellness, sustainability, and premiumization.

Let me start with our recent launches, which have hit the ground running. First, our "VitaGlow" plant-based beverage line under the PureHarvest umbrella. Launched in North America and Europe in Q2, this zero-sugar, high-protein almond-oat blend targets the $15B alt-dairy segment, where we're seeing 8-10% CAGR per Euromonitor. Initial results are stellar: we've achieved 85% ACV distribution in the U.S. top 50 markets within 12 weeks, with velocity at 12 units per store per week—double the category average for new SKUs. Trial rates are at 28% among health-conscious millennials, per Kantar data, and repeat purchase is holding at 45% after 30 days. This has already generated $45 million in incremental sales in Q3, contributing 2 points to our overall organic growth, and we're on track for $200 million annually. It's gaining share from incumbents like Silk and Oatly, with early e-commerce sell-through on Amazon exceeding 4x our internal targets.

Second, in snacks—our largest category at 35% of revenue—our "CrunchVital" seed-based crisp line launched across APAC and LATAM. Formulated with upcycled chia and quinoa for a clean-label, gut-health profile, it taps into the $50B global healthy snacking boom, fueled by post-COVID convenience demands. In Southeast Asia, we've secured 65% ACV in modern trade channels like 7-Eleven and Tesco, driving 18% market share in the seed crisp subcategory within three months. Q3 sales hit $32 million, a 150% acceleration from launch week one, with household penetration up 12 points to 15% in pilot markets per local IRI scans. Margins are robust at 35% gross, thanks to localized sourcing that cut supply chain costs by 20%. This is particularly resonant in LATAM, where inflation-hit consumers are trading up to nutrient-dense options amid 7% food CPI pressures.

On the personal care front, "EcoShield" natural insect repellents under FreshGuard rolled out in Europe and North America. Leveraging bio-based actives from essential oils—think citronella and eucalyptus hybrids—this addresses the $8B DEET-alternative market growing at 12% annually. Distribution stands at 72% ACV in key U.S. retailers like Walmart and Target, with sell-through velocity at 9 units per store per week. Q3 added $28 million in sales, boosting category growth by 9 points. Notably, in Europe, where EU Green Deal regs are pushing chemical-free formulations, we've seen 22% trial among families, outpacing Sawyer and Repel per GfK panel data.

These launches aren't one-offs; they're the output of a $450 million annual R&D investment—up 15% YoY—representing 3.5% of sales, in line with peers like P&G and Unilever. Our innovation engine is structured around three pillars: Consumer-Led Insights, Tech-Enabled Formulation, and Sustainable Sourcing. On insights, we've doubled down on AI-driven analytics via our partnership with NielsenIQ, processing 10 petabytes of shopper data annually to predict trends like "functional indulgence"—e.g., low-cal treats with nootropics. Technically, we're pioneering precision fermentation for protein isolates, akin to Perfect Day's dairy tech, which slashes production costs by 30% while hitting 95% plant-based purity. Sustainability-wise, 80% of our pipeline uses regenerative agriculture; for instance, our quinoa supply in Peru is carbon-neutral certified, reducing Scope 3 emissions by 25% versus conventional grains.

Turning to the pipeline, we have 45 SKUs in various stages, with 20 slated for launch in FY25. Expected contribution: $750 million in new product revenue, or 8-10% of total sales, with a pipeline IRR of 25% based on NPV modeling. Highlights include: Q4 NA Launch "BlissBar" mood-boosting protein bars with adaptogens like ashwagandha, targeting the $6B functional confectionery space. Pilot tests show 35% repeat rates; projected $150M run-rate. H1 APAC Rollout "HydraPure" electrolyte-infused waters with electrolytes from seaweed extracts, competing in the $20B hydration market dominated by Prime and Gatorade. Early velocity forecasts: 15 units/store/week. EM Focus: In India and Brazil, "NutriBloom" fortified staples—think rice-milk hybrids with micronutrients—to combat malnutrition while premiumizing staples. Partnerships with local co-ops ensure 40% cost savings.

Regionally, North America remains our innovation powerhouse, delivering 60% of new product sales with 14% growth, fueled by e-commerce (now 25% of NP sales via DTC and Shopify integrations). Europe is at 20% growth, riding regulatory tailwinds for clean beauty and eco-packaging—our recyclable pouches have won EU Ecolabel approval. APAC and LATAM are the stars for volume, up 22% and 18% respectively, as urban millennials drive premium snacking amid rising disposable incomes (APAC middle class expanding 5% YoY per World Bank). Challenges persist in EMEA inflation, but our pricing elasticity modeling shows 70% pass-through without volume loss.

Strategically, we're rationalizing our portfolio: sunsetting 15% of legacy SKUs with <5% velocity to fund high-growth innovations, echoing Colgate's playbook. We're also accelerating DTC and D2C pilots—our app-based subscription for VitaGlow has 50K users, with LTV at $120 versus $40 CAC. Looking ahead, innovation will drive 40% of our 2024-2026 EPS growth, supported by 5-7% organic sales CAGR. Risks like raw material volatility (e.g., almond prices up 10% on drought) are mitigated via hedging and alt-ingredients.

In summary on this front, our launches are proving the power of disciplined innovation in a maturing CPG landscape. We're not just keeping pace with disruptors like Chobani or RXBAR—we're setting the pace.

I'll now turn to our gross margin outlook for the back half of the fiscal year and into FY '25, which remains a cornerstone of our margin expansion algorithm as we navigate a dynamic CPG landscape. As you heard earlier, Q3 delivered a gross margin of 48.2%, up 190 basis points year-over-year, driven by disciplined pricing, robust gross productivity, and a favorable input cost environment—particularly in dairy and edible oils. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of sequential expansion, putting us ahead of our long-term target of 48% by FY '26.

For Q4, we guide gross margins to 48.5% to 49.0%, representing 30 to 80 basis points of sequential improvement. Full-year FY '24 guidance is tightened to 48.8% to 49.2%, implying roughly 250 basis points of expansion versus prior year. Looking to FY '25, we expect further acceleration to 49.5% to 50.0%, supported by structural levers that are now fully embedded in our P&L.

Let me unpack the key assumptions underpinning this guidance, categorized by driver for clarity.

Pricing Discipline, expected +120 bps contribution FY '24: We've realized 5.8% organic pricing in the first half, in line with peers like Mondelez and Hershey amid sustained inflation pass-through. For Q4 and FY '24, we assume 3-4% pricing realization globally, tapering from elevated levels but still above historical norms. This reflects our list-to-street elasticity model, where we've captured 85% of list price increases net of promotion and trade spend—better than the industry average of 70-75%. Key actions include targeted AUR hikes on core power brands like our NutriCrunch snack line (up 6% YoY) and PureGlow skincare franchise, offsetting consumer downtrading pressures seen in mass channels. In FY '25, pricing moderates to 2-3% as inflation eases, but we'll protect share through everyday low pricing in high-velocity SKUs.

Input Cost Environment, headwind of -20 bps FY '24; tailwind +50 bps FY '25: Commodity markets remain volatile, but our hedging book—covering 70% of FY '24 needs—positions us well. We assume a 2-3% input cost inflation for FY '24, down from 8% last year, with deflation in key inputs: Dairy and sugars -4% QoQ, mirroring USDA forecasts and benefiting our yogurt and beverage portfolios. Edible oils like palm and soy flat to -2%, thanks to bumper South American harvests. Cocoa and coffee +15-20% headwind, echoing Mondelez's warnings, but mitigated by our 12-month forward contracts at $4,200/ton for cocoa (vs. spot at $5,800).

Regionally: North America sees modest 1% inflation due to stable wheat and corn; EMEA faces 4% pressure from energy-linked ag inputs amid Ukraine ripple effects; APAC benefits from -3% rice deflation in Indonesia and India; LatAm hedges offset 5% local currency volatility in Brazil coffee. For FY '25, we project overall deflation of 1-2%, accelerating margin leverage.

Gross Productivity Savings, tailwind +110 bps FY '24: Our "CPG Efficiency 2.0" program—now in Phase III—delivers $450 million in structural savings this year, or 2.1% of COGS, on track with Unilever's "Productivity Program" benchmarks. Breakdown: Supply chain optimization 40% of savings ($180M), via AI-driven network redesign (e.g., consolidating 15 DCs to 10, cutting freight 12% with route optimization algorithms akin to PepsiCo's playbook). Precision agriculture pilots in cocoa sourcing with partners like Barry Callebaut yield 8% yield improvements. Manufacturing excellence 35% ($160M) from zero-based manufacturing, including variable speed drives on lines reducing energy 15%, and robotics in high-labor pouch packaging (ROI <18 months). Procurement leverage 25% ($110M) through strategic sourcing alliances, like our palm oil RSPO-certified consortium locking in 5% below-market rates.

These are durable, with 80% recurring into FY '25.

Volume/Mix Dynamics +30 bps FY '24: We assume 2.0-2.5% organic volume growth in H2, with mix +1.5% from premiumization: premium snacks and clean-label personal care now 28% of portfolio (up from 22% two years ago), echoing P&G's "Superiority Strategy." Offsets include 1-2% unfavorable channel mix from e-comm growth (higher fulfillment costs) and private label share erosion in Europe (e.g., Aldi/Lidl gaining 50 bps in laundry).

Currency and Other neutral to +10 bps: FX headwinds ease to 50 bps for FY '24 (EUR/USD at 1.08, BRL at 5.50), hedged 60%. Tariff risks minimal post-USMCA tweaks.

Key Risks and Sensitivities: This guidance assumes no major FX shocks (>5% move), commodity spikes (e.g., cocoa >$6,500/ton), or supply disruptions (e.g., Red Sea routing adds 3-5% to APAC freight). Elasticity risk: if volumes soften >2% due to recessionary pressures—like the 1.5% US CPG volume dip in Q1—we could see 20-30 bps margin pressure, offset by pricing agility. Sustainability capex ($100M FY '24) is embedded, supporting Scope 3 reductions that unlock retailer premiums (e.g., Walmart's "Gigaton" incentives).

In summary, our gross margin trajectory reflects a balanced algorithm: pricing tailwinds transitioning to productivity dominance, positioning GCB for industry-leading expansion. This funds our 12-14% operating margin goal and 10%+ EPS CAGR through the cycle.

Turning to outlook: For Q4, we expect organic sales growth of 4.5-5.5%, with volumes +1.5-2.5% as holiday promotions ramp. Full-year FY24 organic growth now guided to 5.5-6.0% (up from 4-5.5%), underlying EPS $6.45-6.55 (midpoint +9% YoY), and core operating margin 18.0-18.5%. For FY25, we're targeting organic growth of 4-6%, EPS growth of 7-9%, and free cash flow conversion above 95%, assuming moderating inflation (commodities down 10-15% YoY) but persistent FX volatility—we now model a $0.10-0.15 negative EPS impact from USD strength.

Risks include potential U.S. recessionary pullback in non-essentials, where we'd lean on our 70/30 staples/discretionary mix, and supply chain disruptions from Red Sea rerouting, which we've mitigated with +20% inventory buffers. On the upside, our $2.5 billion innovation pipeline—including plant-based PeakMeat alternatives launching Q1—positions us to capture health trends, much like Beyond Meat's early momentum but with our scale.

In summary, Q3 underscores GCB's ability to navigate volatility through superior execution, tech leverage, and a bulletproof portfolio. We're proud of delivering shareholder value while investing for sustainable growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, John. Inflation continues to shape consumer behavior, but our Everyday Essentials portfolio has proven resilient. Shoppers are prioritizing staples like our PeakPure waters and PeakClean detergents, where we've seen steady volumes despite broader CPG softness. In non-essentials, there's some downtrading to private labels, but our pricing discipline—3-4% organic in H2—and premium innovations like VitaGlow have maintained elasticity, with 85% list-to-street capture. Premium snacks and clean beauty are holding up among millennials, up 14% in North America, as health trends trump price sensitivity. Regionally, EMEA's high inflation drove 8.2% growth via value engineering, and APAC's rebound shows urban consumers trading up. We're monitoring recession risks but confident in our 70/30 staples mix buffering any pullback.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wong with JPMorgan.

Emily Wong:
Regarding your new product VitaGlow, what are the projections for its market impact?

Sarah Lopez:
Hi Emily, great question on VitaGlow. This plant-based beverage is off to a strong start, with $45 million in Q3 sales already contributing 2 points to organic growth, and we're projecting a $200 million annual run-rate. In the $15B alt-dairy space, it's gaining share from Silk and Oatly, with 85% ACV in U.S. top markets, 12 units per store weekly velocity—double category norms—and 45% repeat rates. E-commerce is crushing it at 4x targets on Amazon. Market impact-wise, expect 1-2 share points in alt-dairy by FY25 end, driven by our pipeline synergies like HydraPure extensions. Margins at 40%+ support reinvestment, and with 28% trial among millennials, it's set to disrupt with sustainability creds unlocking retailer slots.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Harris with Barclays.

Bob Harris:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Bob. Promotional spending was up 12% in trade spend as a percentage of our response strategy, funding retailer promotions without eroding net pricing. We layered this into 35% of the portfolio via EDLP resets, preserving ASP at $3.42, up 5.2% YoY. This countered aggressive BOGOs from Unilever and P&G, like Rexona's deals, while boosting ACV to 92.6%. In snacks and laundry, it reversed volume dips—e.g., Gain Flings gained 110 bps distribution. Overall, it supported 6.2% organic growth, with A&P at $450 million, 40% digital for higher ROI. FY24 guide embeds 10-12% of sales in total promo, tapering as productivity kicks in.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Lisa Chen for closing remarks.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
